An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 36 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.text:
I ran the suite: 39/39 pass. Line counts are fine: app.js 150, index.html 41, page.test.mjs 232, page-static.test.mjs 79, fake-dom.mjs 87.

**Spec check, public/index.html and public/app.js**
I checked every Page line (spec lines 46-66) and the code meets all of them.
- **HTML:** title and h1 are right, the form has `novalidate`, all five fields have labels, `#error` is empty, there is no `<option>` and no room names, and no `http://` or `https://` appears.
- **Script tag:** it is the last element in body, with no `type`, `defer` or `async`.
- **Classic script:** no `import`/`export`, and setup runs at once.
- **Browser APIs:** only the line-50 whitelist is used (`fetch` with method/headers/body, `status`, `json()`, `getElementById`, `createElement`, `textContent`/`value`/`type`/`disabled`/`append`/`replaceChildren`/`addEventListener`, `preventDefault`).
- **Replies:** a 204 never calls `json()` (app.js:32). A non-204 reply with bad JSON falls into the catch and counts as no reply.
- **Overlapping list fetches:** the generation counter is checked before anything is applied (app.js:86-93).
- **Book:** it is re-enabled on the first line after the await (app.js:129), before anything else.
- **Cancel:** with no reply it does not fetch the list again. The list URL keeps the date unchanged.

**Code findings**
- public/app.js:25-29: `request` builds `options` and then adds `headers` and `body` to it afterwards. The project rule is to return new objects, so this should be one spread object.
- public/app.js:59 and :98: `result.body.rooms.map` and `result.body.bookings.length` assume the 200 body has the right shape. If it doesn't, a TypeError is thrown inside a promise nobody awaits (app.js:148-149, 112, 136, 141, 145). Nothing catches it and the user sees nothing. Treat a wrong shape the same as an error status, or catch at the call sites.

**Test gaps**
app.js runs inside `vm`, so the coverage tool can't measure it. Reading the code against the tests, these spec requirements have no test:
- **List fetch errors (spec line 60):** no test covers a list fetch that is the latest one and gets an error status or no reply. The error branch at app.js:94-96 never runs for the list, because in both overlap tests the failing fetch is the out-of-date one. Code that cleared the list on error would pass.
- **List success leaves `#error` alone:** untested. Code that clears `#error` on success would pass.
- **Earlier fetch succeeds after a later one:** the overlap tests only cover an earlier error or rejection. Code that ignored only out-of-date errors would pass.
- **"Book enabled before anything else happens":** this is only checked after `flush()`. Code that re-enabled Book after setting `#error` or after starting the list fetch would pass.
- **POST 201 with bad JSON counts as no reply:** only tested for rooms.
- **Cancel 404 re-enables the button:** not asserted.

The static test uses a list of banned words, while the spec gives a list of allowed APIs. The vm sandbox, which only provides `document` and `fetch`, covers most of the gap, so this is acceptable.

Tests (6) is under your bar of 7, so this fails.

## GRADE
Overall: 8.6/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 9 — clear small functions in one IIFE; `request` adds to `options` after building it instead of making one new object
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent (loadList, bookingItem, showOutcomeError, listGeneration)
duplication: 9 — shared request/errorMessage/showOutcomeError helpers; only small repeated null-or-not-ok checks
size: 10 — all files well under 400 lines, every function under 25 lines
errors: 8 — no-reply/error-status/204/bad-JSON handled exactly; a wrong-shape 200 body throws in a promise nobody awaits
tests: 6 — list-fetch error and no-reply branch never runs; "success leaves #error alone", earlier success after a later one, Book-enabled-first ordering and POST bad JSON untested
security: 10 — textContent/append only, no HTML injection, path-only URLs, no secrets
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs; comments are explanatory
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:113 add tests where the latest list fetch gets 500 `{error:'boom'}` and where it gets no reply: assert `#error` shows the message and `#booking-list` children are unchanged from a previously rendered list
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:84 add a test that sets `#error` to 'old', lets a list fetch succeed, and asserts `#error` is still 'old'
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:101 add an overlap case where the earlier fetch succeeds after the later one with different bookings; assert the list shows the later result
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:155 assert Book is already enabled when the follow-up list fetch starts (check `els.book.disabled` inside the fake fetch at the moment calls[3] is pushed) and when `#error` is set on 409
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:188 add a POST 201 test with `badJson: true` that expects `Could not reach the server.`, title kept and no list fetch
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:223 assert `button.disabled === false` after the Cancel 404
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/public/app.js:25 build the fetch options as one new object, e.g. `const options = payload === undefined ? { method } : { method, headers: {...}, body: JSON.stringify(payload) };`
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/public/app.js:59 check `Array.isArray(result.body?.rooms)` (same for `bookings` at :98) and show `Request failed.` instead of throwing in a promise nobody awaits
